Bayesian normal model

Source: vignettes/normal-priors.Rmd
normal-priors.Rmd

Live demo

Open this example in Shinylive

This example uses two interactive priors for a Normal likelihood:

\[ y_i \mid \mu, \sigma^2 \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2), \]

\[ \mu \sim \mathcal{N}(m_0, s_0^2), \qquad \sigma^2 \sim \operatorname{InverseGamma}(\alpha_0, \beta_0). \]

The posterior is proportional to likelihood times priors:

\[ p(\mu, \sigma^2 \mid y) \propto p(y \mid \mu, \sigma^2)\, p(\mu)\, p(\sigma^2). \]

The app reveals observations from the real mtcars$mpg data, evaluates the posterior on a small deterministic grid, then integrates the joint surface numerically to obtain marginal posterior densities for \(\mu\) and \(\sigma^2\). This keeps the example transparent and avoids an MCMC dependency.

The two priors are ordinary modist_input() controls:

modist_input(
  "mu_prior",
  family = "normal",
  value = list(mu = 20, sigma = 5)
)

modist_input(
  "variance_prior",
  family = "inversegamma",
  value = list(alpha = 5, beta = 120)
)

Run it locally with:

shiny::runApp(
  system.file("examples/normal-priors", package = "shinymodist")
)
